name: OpenBlog SEO Pipeline
description: Runs the upstream OpenBlog 5-stage pipeline to generate grounded SEO articles, images, verified URLs, internal links, and export artifacts.
long_description:
This worker bundles and runs the real federicodeponte/openblog engine inside
the Workeros E2B sandbox. It executes the upstream 5-stage pipeline:
Set Context, Blog Generation plus Images, Quality Check, URL Verification,
and Internal Links.

The run uses GEMINI_API_KEY from Workeros secrets, fetches company context
and sitemap data over the network, runs Gemini 3 Flash with Google Search
grounding, requests Imagen article images unless explicitly disabled, and
writes the exported article files plus raw pipeline metadata. Missing images
or missing requested export formats are returned as an explicit failed run
with an export report, not hidden as a successful partial result.
use_cases: Generate a complete SEO article from a company URL and one or more target keywords.
Produce grounded content with URL verification, internal links, and structured raw output.
Stress-test the full OpenBlog engine, including image generation and export formats, inside E2B.

}

Company URL + target keywords
  -> run Stage 1 company context and sitemap discovery
  -> run Stage 2 article generation plus Imagen images
  -> run Stage 3 quality fixes

name: Outbound approval demo
description: Demonstrates the two-run HITL approval pattern. Run 1 drafts an outbound message and proposes it for approval. Run 2 (spawned after approval) executes the approved message by writing it to a context file.
long_description:
This worker proves the S47 HITL approval flow end-to-end.

Phase 1 (run 1): draft an outbound message for a given prospect and emit
decision_required so a human can review before anything is sent.

Phase 2 (run 2): reads inputs.decision and inputs.approved_output, then
executes the approved message and records the side-effect as the output
fields sent=true + sent_message.

Idempotency constraint: only run 2 fires the side-effect. Run 1 NEVER
sends anything.
use_cases: Approve outbound recruiting emails before they reach candidates.
Gate any worker side-effect behind a human decision step.
Test the two-run HITL respawn flow in a safe, harmless way.
how_it_works:
Run 1: draft message -> emit decision_required -> land PENDING_APPROVAL
Human: approve (optionally edit) or reject via /approvals
Run 2 (spawned): read approved_output -> record sent=true + sent_message

inputs.name: decision
inputs.label: Approval decision (set by system on run 2)
inputs.description: Set to "approved" by the approval system when spawning run 2.

inputs.name: approved_output
inputs.label: Approved output (set by system on run 2)
inputs.description: The approved (possibly edited) output from run 1.

name: AI News Discord Digester
description: Fetches top AI news every 60 minutes, summarizes three stories, and posts a digest to Discord.
long_description:
Automatically keeps your Discord server updated with the latest AI news.
Every five minutes, the worker searches the web for recent AI-related news
from the last 24 hours, selects the top three stories, and writes a concise
three-bullet digest. Each bullet includes a one-line summary and a direct
link to the article, which is then posted into your chosen Discord channel.  

This is useful for AI-focused communities, research groups, or teams who
want a lightweight, continuous feed of relevant AI developments without
leaving Discord.
use_cases: Keep an AI-focused Discord community updated with fresh news.
Provide a lightweight AI news ticker in a team server.
Monitor major AI announcements without checking news sites manually.
Support daily AI research by surfacing key headlines in chat.
Give newcomers a rolling snapshot of current AI developments.
example_output:
**Top AI News (last 24h)**
- [Major model release announced](https://example.com/story1) — New frontier model claims state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks.
- [Regulator proposes AI rules](https://example.com/story2) — Draft framework targets transparency and safety requirements for high-risk systems.
- [Startup raises funding for AI tool](https://example.com/story3) — Company secures Series B to expand its AI-powered productivity platform.
how_it_works:
Scheduled trigger every 5 minutes
  -> query a news/search API for AI news from the last 24 hours
  -> rank and select the top three stories
  -> format a three-bullet Discord-friendly digest with links
  -> post the digest message to the configured Discord channel

use_cases: Get a single Slack message each day with your most important GitHub notifications.
Stay on top of review requests and mentions without living in the GitHub UI.
Reduce GitHub notification overload by focusing on a small, ranked subset.
Share a summary of your team's most important notifications in a Slack channel.
Quickly scan what needs your attention before standup or EOD.

example_input.additional_instructions: Group by repo, highlight PRs first, and keep the summary under 12 lines.

example_output:
## GitHub Notification Digest (last 24h)

**Pull Requests (7)**
- [acme/webapp] #342 _Add OAuth callback logging_ — **review requested** from you — 3h ago
- [acme/api] #781 _Refactor billing webhook_ — **mention** in a comment — 6h ago

**Issues (3)**
- [acme/webapp] #1290 _Login intermittently failing_ — **assigned** to you — 20h ago

Posted to Slack channel `#github-notifications`.
how_it_works:
Scheduled trigger (daily at 09:00 UTC)
  -> Use GitHub connection to fetch notifications within the look-back window
  -> Rank by importance (review requests, mentions, assignments) and recency
  -> Group and format into a concise markdown digest
  -> Post the digest to the configured Slack channel via Slack connection
  -> Return the markdown digest and Slack message timestamp (if available)

name: Person News Sentiment Brief
description: Finds recent news about a person and returns a balanced brief with positive and negative points
long_description:
Searches recent public news about the person you provide and turns the findings into a concise brief.

The output includes a latest-news summary, three positive points, two negative points, and source links so you can review the evidence.

Review recent public coverage before a meeting.
Summarize balanced news signals for research.
